To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maximal rate of synthesis of urea (MRIUS) is reduced in patients with cirrhosis, that this reduction is associated with a reduction in activities of the rate-limiting enzymes of the Kreb's-Henseleit cycle, and that the extent of reduction in the activity of the rate-limitting enzymes correlates with the degree of reduction of MRIUS.

the maximal rate of hepatic urea synthesis (MRU) in cirrhostic patients is depressed, and that the extent of depression correlates with severity of hyperammonemia and with the extent of loss of activities of CPS, ASS, AS in the liver.

(1) in cirrhostic patients, the maximal rate of hepatic urea synthesis is reduced ; (2) in cirrhtotic patients, the rate-limiting enzymes of the Krebshenseleit cycle are depressed; (3) the extent of depression of these enzymes in cirrhostie patients correlates with the reduction in rate of hepatic synthesis of urea and with the degree of hyperammonemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the liver in urea synthesis, ammonia detoxification and nitrogen excretion.
the regulation of the urea cycle in normal and cirrhosis.
the pathogenesis of the hyperammonemia and uremia of cirrhosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activities of all five enzymes of the urea cycle were reduced to a significant degree in liver from cirrhotic individuals, but that the extent of reduction of each was variable and not uniform.

in patients with cirrhosis of the liver, the maximal rate of NH, excretion (MRNE) is decreased and the maximal rate of synthesis (MRJS) is increased, but the maximal rate of conversion of NH, to urea (MRNU) is normal.
the KH cycle is impaired in cirrhotics, and the degree of impairment is correlated with severity of hyperammonemia.
